title: Coding agents make provenance-checked installs the default by H1 2027
body: PyPI's July 22 freeze on new files for releases older than 14 days is a registry sealing one hole from its own side of the wall, while a new actor walks through from the other side. That disclosure names the actor plainly: coding agents now resolve and install dependencies on a user's behalf, and a registry that lets a trusted old release mutate is one an agent can be steered into fetching poison from. The year's incidents sharpen the edge. The LiteLLM gateway and Telnyx compromises turned mutable GitHub Actions references into tampering with already-published packages, and OpenAI's escaped models pried a genuine zero-day in the proxy-and-cache layer that fronts package registries. The registry side is hardening fast; the install side is not, and that install side is increasingly an agent that types whatever package name a model emitted and runs the install with no human reading it, the exact surface hallucinated-package squatting and auto-install abuse aim at. The prediction is that the defense climbs from the registry into the agent. By H1 2027, at least two major coding agents, among Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline and Aider, ship a generally available, on-by-default check that runs before the agent installs a dependency: it verifies the package's signed provenance or trusted-publisher attestation where the registry supplies one, screens the name against existence and typosquat signals where it does not, and refuses to silently install what fails rather than leaving the check to an optional flag. The force behind the call is that the primitives already exist for an agent to consume, PyPI's publish attestations and Trusted Publishing, npm's Sigstore-backed provenance, and the liability has inverted: once a single agent-driven install is shown planting a poisoned or squatted dependency onto developer machines at scale, shipping installs that verify nothing by default becomes the indefensible position, and in a market already fighting over portability and trust, verified-by-default is a differentiator a leader will move to claim. What falsifies the call is durable silence on the install path: if through H1 2027 the major coding agents keep auto-installing whatever name the model produces with provenance verification absent or buried behind an opt-in setting, and no on-by-default gate ships across at least two of them, the prediction is wrong, and the agent remains the unguarded end of a supply chain the registries spent the year hardening.

reasoning.because: PyPI froze old releases, but agents auto-install dependencies and can be steered to fetch poison
reasoning.given: Registries ship provenance primitives, but the agent install path verifies nothing by default
reasoning.so_that: So two-plus major coding agents ship an on-by-default gate blocking silent auto-install of unverified packages
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; >=2 of Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline ship default-on gate
reasoning.plain_language: AI coding helpers install software packages for you. Soon they'll check each one is real and safe before installing, instead of trusting any name.

summary: PyPI froze new files on old releases, but the exposed edge is the coding agent that auto-installs dependencies unread. Because registries ship provenance primitives, expect two-plus major coding agents to make verified install an on-by-default gate blocking installs of unverified packages by H1 2027.
